newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's pension funds grew 8.1 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's pension funds grew 8.1 pct in January.

text.p: The assets of Colombia's private pension funds grew by 8.1 percent in January to a total of 872 billion pesos, the Banking Superintendency said.
It said the growth was fueled, at least in part, by a 2.0 percent increase in the number of affiliates to a total of just over 2 million people.

Colombia established its private pension fund system in 1994. A total of eight funds now operate in the country, led by Porvenir, which belongs to industrialist Luis Carlos Sarmiento, Proteccion of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate and Colfondos of the Santo Domingo industrial group.

Colombia's private pension fund assets are relatively small compared to other countries in the region. But they are growing rapidly and some analysts estimate they could reach about $2 billion by early next year.
Brokers say the funds have also become active players in Colombia's stock market this year and contributed to a sharp run- up in share prices in January.
